system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

brief.intent: the woman in the technical jacket rides the dragon into an epic battleground, cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements

cards.summary: A dark, photorealistic character reference sheet for one adult person with an undercut and small topknot, dressed in a black tactical jacket, black pants, and combat boots; it includes a rainy rooftop hero shot, front/side/back turnaround views, and face, collar, hands, and boots detail panels.

subjects.descriptor: Adult person shown consistently across all panels
attributes: short dark hair with shaved sides and a small topknot
black high-collared tactical-style jacket with strap and buckle details
black top
black pants
black lace-up combat boots
pose: hero panel: standing with body facing forward and head turned toward frame left
front panel: standing upright facing camera with arms at sides
side profile panel: standing in profile facing frame left
back panel: standing facing away with arms at sides
face close-up: facing camera with a neutral expression
hands close-up: fingers relaxed
boots close-up: boots shown standing

cards.environment: Top panel: rainy rooftop or industrial walkway at night with metal railings, wet reflective ground, dark buildings, and blurred city lights. Lower panels: dark studio-like backdrop.
cards.lighting: Top panel: cool blue night ambience mixed with warm amber practical lights and wet-surface reflections. Lower panels: low-key studio lighting with soft highlights on the face and clothing.
cards.framing: Reference-sheet layout: one wide cinematic hero image at top, three full-body turnaround views in a row, and four close-up detail panels along the bottom.
cards.style: Photorealistic cinematic character concept/reference sheet with a dark, rain-soaked urban tactical aesthetic.

cards.summary: A dark-fantasy dragon reference sheet combining one large cinematic scene with labeled front, side, and rear views plus close-up studies of the head, wing membrane, foot, and scales.

subjects.descriptor: Large black dragon with horns, spines, membranous wings, clawed feet, and a long tail
attributes: quadrupedal body
charcoal-black overlapping scales with faint blue-green sheen
long pale ridged horns swept backward
multiple spikes along the head, neck, and back
large dark membranous wings with visible veining
long tail
clawed feet with large curved talons
small orange eye
pose: top scene: crouched low on rocky ground with wings partly raised
front and rear views: standing with wings spread
side profile: body extended horizontally with wings extended backward
head close-up: head angled toward the viewer with one eye visible

cards.environment: Volcanic rocky terrain with shallow reflective water, jagged crags, distant ember glow, and a dark hazy sky in the large top scene; the lower view and detail panels use plain dark backgrounds.
cards.lighting: Low-key and moody, with the dragon mostly in dark shadow, pale horn and claw highlights, cool blue-green scale reflections, and warm orange ember light in the background.
cards.framing: Composite reference-sheet layout: a wide hero image across the top, three full-body views in the middle row, and four detail panels in the bottom row, separated by thin dark dividers.
cards.style: Dark-fantasy creature concept art and photorealistic digital painting with cinematic presentation.

rendering_permission.reasoning: The request describes scene content and adds a descriptive style tag (“cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements”) but does not grammatically instruct a rendering transformation or specify a complete target rendition operation. This is descriptive metadata appended to scene action, not authorization to depart from the attached visual reference’s rendering.

medium_decision.retained_style: Photorealistic cinematic with a dark, rain-soaked urban tactical aesthetic
medium_decision.reasoning: The host rendering_permission is preserve, so no rendering transformation is authorized. The request adds scene action and a descriptive cinematic/Hollywood style tag, but it does not name a complete target rendition or requested coarse rendering family. The first observed content reference is a reference sheet, so retained_style removes sheet/concept packaging while preserving the actual photorealistic cinematic and dark, rain-soaked urban tactical visual traits.
